items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Red Nickels; the name is only introduced by the interviewer in a question about influence.

ctx.x: Because they had bands in the Mal Hallett band in Boston with Pearly Breed, had some wonderful musicians and they played all the Wolverine arrangements. Note for note.

Well, then, the Wolverine influence was very strong in the white element. Yeah. It recalls that Red Nickels wants to culvert. I wonder if that's enough in Indiana that he could have felt that influence. Hard to say. He does show more Bix maybe than anything else, and it's a leader Bix.

I think that when, well, the Indiana influence on everything in this country is kind of peculiar. It's a peculiar state. It's a, the Hoosiers stick together no matter where they go. There may be presents in New York banks and you'll find them at the Hoosier picnic at Coney Island. It's a crazy place. Full of poets, full of, of, when I said hillbilly earlier while we were talking, I didn't quite mean that, but I, I wasn't too far away from it. It's country music. Ragtime, soft shoe.
